sentences.en: Episode Transcript I’d like you to stop whatever you’re doing right now.
sentences.zh: 节目文稿 我希望你停下目前手头上正在做的事情。

sentences.en: No no, I don’t mean like stop so you can give your full attention to this radio show.
sentences.zh: 不不，我不是指停下来好让你能专心听这个广播节目。

sentences.en: I mean, honestly, radio is the perfect medium for multi-tasking — unless maybe you’re using a chainsaw or something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，说实话，广播其实是多任务处理的完美媒介——除非你正在用链锯或者干别的什么。

sentences.en: What I mean is Stop. Whatever. You’re. Doing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，停下。你。手头。在做的事。

sentences.en: As in, doing with your life.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你生活中正在做的事。

sentences.en: Maybe it’s your job. Maybe it’s a relationship that’s curdled.
sentences.zh: 也许是你的工作。也许是一段已经变质的关系。

sentences.en: Maybe there’s some dream project you’ve been working on so long that you can’t even remember what got you all heated up about it in the first place.
sentences.zh: 也许某个你一直在搞的梦想项目，时间久得你甚至都记当初是什么让你对它那么热血沸腾了。

sentences.en: I want to encourage you to just quit. Or at least think about quitting.
sentences.zh: 我想鼓励你直接放弃。或者至少考虑一下放弃。

sentences.en: Why? Well, because everybody else is always saying the opposite.
sentences.zh: 为什么？嗯，因为所有人总是说相反的话。

sentences.en: It’s become so ingrained that we don’t even think about it any more.
sentences.zh: 这种观念已经根深蒂固，以至于我们甚至不再去思考它。

sentences.en: You know: “A quitter never wins and a winner never quits.” You know what I think when I hear people say that?
sentences.zh: 你知道的：“半途而废者永不得胜，永不言弃者终获成功。”你猜我听到别人这么说时是怎么想的？

sentences.en: I think: Are you sure?
sentences.zh: 我在想：你确定吗？

sentences.en: So I hang out with a lot of economists. (I know, you’re envious.) But there are two things they love to talk about that will help us understand quitting.
sentences.zh: 所以我跟许多经济学家混在一起。（我知道，你很羡慕。）但他们喜欢聊的两个话题能帮我们理解放弃。

sentences.en: One is called “sunk cost” and the other is “opportunity cost.” “Sunk cost” is about the past — it’s the time, or money, or sweat equity that you’ve put into something, which makes it hard to abandon.
sentences.zh: 一个是所谓的“沉没成本”，另一个是“机会成本”。“沉没成本”关乎过去——它是你投入到某件事中的时间、金钱或心血，这让你很难放弃它。

sentences.en: “Opportunity cost” is about the future. It means that for every hour or dollar you spend on one thing, you’re giving up the opportunity to spend that hour or dollar on something else — something that might make your life better.
sentences.zh: “机会成本”关乎未来。这意味着你花在某事上的每一个小时或每一美元，都让你放弃了把这小时或美元花在别的事情上的机会——那些可能会让你的生活变得更好的事情。

sentences.en: If only you weren’t so worried about the sunk cost.
sentences.zh: 如果你没那么担心沉没成本就好了。

sentences.en: If only you could quit. Let’s start with the story of a woman we’ll call “Allie.” Back in 1999, when she was about 25, Allie’s life was already what most people would consider pretty successful: I was working for a Fortune 500, large company.
sentences.zh: 如果你能放弃就好了。让我们从一个我们称之为“艾莉（Allie）”的女性的故事开始。早在1999年，当她大约25岁时，艾莉的生活在大多数人看来就已经相当成功了：我在一家财富500强的大公司工作。

sentences.en: What kind of work were you doing? Industrial computer programming.
sentences.zh: 你当时在做什么工作？工业计算机编程。

sentences.en: What kind of money were you making then?
sentences.zh: 你当时能赚多少钱？

sentences.en: You know, 60, 70 thousand dollars a year.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一年6万、7万美元。

sentences.en: And you were living where? I was living in Texas.
sentences.zh: 你住在哪里？我住在德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: OK, so 60 or 70 thousand dollars as a 25-year-old living in Texas goes a pretty long way.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对于一个住在德克萨斯州的25岁年轻人来说，6万或7万美元能花挺久的。

sentences.en: That sounds pretty good. Oh, for sure. And how did you like to spend your money, generally?
sentences.zh: 听起来很不错。哦，当然。总的来说，你喜欢怎么花你的钱？

sentences.en: I think like most 25-year-old women, you know, shoes, and I had a nice place to live and a decent car to drive, so… And how did you like the job?
sentences.zh: 我想就像大多数25岁的女性一样，你知道的，鞋子，我有一个不错的住所，还有一辆像样的车可以开，所以……那你觉得这份工作怎么样？

sentences.en: I never loved it. I am more of a social person, and it requires long, long periods of sitting at a computer desk talking to nobody.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有真正爱过它。我其实是个更喜欢社交的人，而这工作需要长时间、长时间地坐在电脑桌前跟谁都不说话。

sentences.en: I understand that you ended up quitting this job.
sentences.zh: 我听说你最后把这份工作辞了。

sentences.en: In your new pursuit — did you have to take a big pay cut?
sentences.zh: 在你新的追求中——你不得不接受大幅降薪吗？

sentences.en: The new job paid way better. Way better like, 50 percent more?
sentences.zh: 新工作薪水高得多。高得多，比如多百分之五十？

sentences.en: Twice as much?
sentences.zh: 多一倍？

sentences.en: More. Three times as much? Four times as much?
sentences.zh: 更多。多三倍？多四倍？

sentences.en: Somewhere around there. Somewhere around four times as much?
sentences.zh: 差不多吧。差不多是四倍左右？

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe even more. That means, well you must’ve, that means you must’ve had to work way more hours than you worked as a computer programmer then, right?
sentences.zh: 对，可能甚至更多。那意味着，好吧，你一定，那意味着你当时肯定比当程序员时工作时间要长得多吧，对吧？

sentences.en: This is what was so great about it. I had to work a lot less.
sentences.zh: 这就是最棒的地方。我工作少多了。

sentences.en: It must have been very, very, very difficult or unpleasant work, then?
sentences.zh: 那它一定是非常、非常、非常困难或令人不快的工作咯？

sentences.en: Oh, no. I enjoyed my work and enjoyed my free time and of course the extra money allowed me to do a lot of the things I wasn’t able to do before.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。我很享受我的工作，也享受我的闲暇时光，当然，额外的金钱让我能够做很多以前做不到的事情。

sentences.en: So tell me, what was this new work that you found?
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我，你找到的这个新工作是什么？

sentences.en: The new job that I found was that I was a high-end escort.
sentences.zh: 我找到的新工作是，我成了一名高端伴游。

sentences.en: It paid somewhere between 350 to 500 dollars an hour.
sentences.zh: 时薪大概在350到500美元之间。

sentences.en: In retrospect, how do you feel about that decision back then to quit that solid, steady, fairly good-paying job for the life of a high-end escort?
sentences.zh: 回想起来，对于当年放弃那份稳妥、稳定、薪水相当不错的工作去过上高端伴游的生活这个决定，你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: You know, of course it’s always scary to leave behind something that’s legit.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，抛弃一些合法的东西总是让人害怕的。

sentences.en: And go with something that maybe isn’t considered that.
sentences.zh: 然后去选择某种可能不被认为是合法的事情。

sentences.en: I really enjoyed it. I know that it was the right decision for me.
sentences.zh: 我真的很享受。我知道这对我来说是正确的决定。

sentences.en: For me, I don’t have a problem with having sex with strangers.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，跟陌生人发生性关系不是什么大问题。

sentences.en: But it wasn’t something that I felt was demoralizing.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是一件让我觉得有失尊严的事。

sentences.en: And I enjoyed it. I enjoyed my customers; I enjoyed the kindness, and I enjoyed every part of it.
sentences.zh: 我很享受。我很享受我的客户；我享受那种善意，并且我享受其中的每一部分。

sentences.en: All right, so we’re probably starting off on the wrong foot here.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以我们在这里可能一开始就走错了方向。

sentences.en: I encourage you to think about quitting, and the first person we hear from quit a perfectly good job to become a hooker!
sentences.zh: 我鼓励你们考虑放弃，而我们听到的第一个人居然为了当妓女而辞掉了一份相当不错的工作！

sentences.en: But hear me out. My thesis is simple: In our zeal to “tough things out,” to keep our nose to the grindstone, in our zeal to win, we underestimate the upside of quitting.
sentences.zh: 但请听我解释。我的论点很简单：在我们执着于“咬牙坚持”、埋头苦干，在我们对胜利的狂热追求中，我们低估了放弃的好处。

sentences.en: Now full disclosure here: I am a serial quitter.
sentences.zh: 顺便坦白一下：我是一个连续放弃者。

sentences.en: I’ve quit a dream job, with The New York Times; I quit my childhood dream — being a rock star; I even quit a religion.
sentences.zh: 我曾辞掉过《纽约时报》的梦想工作；我放弃过儿时的梦想——当一名摇滚明星；我甚至放弃过一种宗教。

sentences.en: We’ll get to my quits later. First, here’s someone who made headlines when he quit.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后再谈我的放弃经历。首先，是一位因辞职而登上头条的人。

sentences.en: Well, I decided – I mean this was long in coming – I was feeling more and more miserable about not seeing my kids, it was weighing on me to a greater, and greater extent.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我决定——我的意思是这酝酿很久了——我越来越为见不到孩子们而感到痛苦，这给我的压力越来越大，程度也越来越深。

sentences.en: I made the decision that shortly after the election I would leave.
sentences.zh: 我做出了决定，在大选后不久我就会离开。

sentences.en: And then one day I went into the Oval Office and explained to the president that I just felt that I had no choice.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天我走进椭圆形办公室，向总统解释说我只是觉得自己别无选择。

sentences.en: He was very understanding about it. That’s Robert Reich.
sentences.zh: 他对此非常理解。那是罗伯特·赖克（Robert Reich）。

sentences.en: He was the U.S. Secretary of Labor during President Clinton’s first term.
sentences.zh: 他曾是克林顿总统第一任期内的美国劳工部长。

sentences.en: He helped put in place the Family and Medical Leave Act; he raised the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 他帮忙推出了《家庭与医疗假法案》；他提高了最低工资。

sentences.en: On his watch, unemployment fell below 5 percent — the lowest it had been in 20 years!
sentences.zh: 在他任职期间，失业率降至5%以下——这是20年来的最低水平！

sentences.en: Now it’s hard to say how effective any one person in Washington really is, but Time magazine named Reich one of the 10 best Cabinet members of the 20h century.
sentences.zh: 现在很难说华盛顿的某个人到底有多大成效，但《时代》杂志将赖克评为20世纪最佳内阁成员之一。

sentences.en: And then Reich quit. The question for me was well, how do I alert my employees and the segment of the public that felt that they were relying on me in some way?
sentences.zh: 然后赖克辞职了。对我的问题是，好吧，我该如何提醒我的员工以及那些觉得自己某种程度上依赖我的公众？

sentences.en: How did I handle it publicly? It’s a delicate matter.
sentences.zh: 我该如何公开处理此事？这是一个微妙的问题。

sentences.en: I decided that I would write an op-ed for The New York Times, “My Personal Family Leave Act.” I had been responsible for implementing the Family and Medical Leave Act that actually was passed years before.
sentences.zh: 我决定为《纽约时报》写一篇专栏文章，“我个人的家庭假法案”。我曾负责实施几年前实际通过的《家庭与医疗假法案》。

sentences.en: And it seems to me important to say to men as well as women that it is OK to leave your job.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，对男性和女性同样重要的是，离开工作岗位是没有问题的。

sentences.en: Here, as Reich wrote it, was his dilemma: “You love your job and you love your family, and you desperately want more of both.” His wife and two teenage sons were back in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 正如赖克当时所写，他的两难境地是：“你热爱你的工作，你也热爱你的家庭，你极度渴望拥有更多的时间陪伴两者。”他的妻子和两个十几岁的儿子远在马萨诸塞州剑桥。

sentences.en: And he was — well, he could have been anywhere.
sentences.zh: 而他——嗯，他本可以去任何地方。

sentences.en: You know the other cabinet officers go to wonderful locations around the world, Paris, London, Shanghai, and elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其他内阁官员会去世界各地的好地方，巴黎、伦敦、上海等等。

sentences.en: The Secretary of Labor goes to Toledo, Ohio, or maybe St.
sentences.zh: 劳工部长则要去俄亥俄州托莱多，或者如果是个好日子的话，也许去圣路易斯。

sentences.en: Louis if it’s really a great day. The funny thing is no one believed Reich quit because he actually wanted to spend more time with his family.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，没有人相信赖克辞职是因为他真的想花更多时间陪家人。

sentences.en: That’s what CEOs say when they’re booted.
sentences.zh: 那是CEO们被炒鱿鱼时才会说的话。

sentences.en: But people — especially male people — don’t quit White House jobs to do that.
sentences.zh: 但人们——尤其是男性——不会为了这个而辞掉白宫的工作。

sentences.en: But Reich really meant it! As he saw it, there was a big upside to quitting.
sentences.zh: 但赖克是认真的！在他看来，放弃有很大的好处。

sentences.en: It was exactly the right move. I think if I had not done it I would have regretted it all my life.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是正确的举动。我想如果我没有这么做，我这一辈子都会后悔的。

sentences.en: I wouldn’t have spent any time – the boys then would have gone off to college, off to their careers, you know I just wouldn’t have those years.
sentences.zh: 我不会花时间陪他们——男孩们当时会上大学，去追求各自的职业生涯，你知道的，我只是会错过那些年。

sentences.en: At the same time, I think I was fooling myself a little bit in thinking that young teenage boys would drop everything when their father came home and say, “Oh dad it’s great to have you, let’s play!” No, they were very happy to have me there but then they said, “But dad, we’re going off with our friends.” So, I kind of would trail around after them a little bit with my metaphoric tail between my legs and try to, you know, well say, “Wouldn’t you like to play?
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我认为自己有点自欺欺人，以为十几岁的男孩子会在父亲回家时放下手头的一切，然后说：“哦，爸爸，有你太棒了，我们玩吧！”不，他们很高兴我在那儿，但接着他们会说：“但是爸爸，我们要和朋友们出去了。”所以，我有点像夹着尾巴（寓意上）跟在他们后面晃悠，然后试着，你知道的，就说：“你们不想玩吗？

sentences.en: How about going to a baseball game?” Robert Reich quit what was, for him, a dream job: running the Department of Labor of the United States.
sentences.zh: 去棒球场怎么样？”罗伯特赖克放弃了对他而言的梦想工作：管理美国劳工部。

sentences.en: But tell me the truth — when you were a kid, did you dream of running the Department of Labor?
sentences.zh: 但说实话——当你还是个孩子的时候，你梦想过管理劳工部吗？

sentences.en: Or maybe you had a dream that sounded more like this.
sentences.zh: 或者你也许做过听起来更像这样的梦。

sentences.en: You get a phone call that says, “How’s it feel to be the next member of the Houston Astros?’”It’s a dream come true.
sentences.zh: 你接到一个电话，上面说：“成为休斯敦太空人队的一员感觉如何？”梦想成真了。

sentences.en: So I ended up signing. I got some money to pay for school, and went straight to Martinsville at 18.
sentences.zh: 所以我最终签约了。我得到了一些钱来支付学费，并在18岁时直奔马丁斯维尔。

sentences.en: That’s Justin Humphries. Not long ago, he was considered one of the best young baseball players in the country — a big power-hitter from a suburb of Houston.
sentences.zh: 那是贾斯汀·汉弗莱斯（Justin Humphries）。不久前，他被认为是全国最好的年轻棒球运动员之一——来自休斯敦郊区的一个强力击球手。

sentences.en: Getting drafted by the hometown Astros was especially sweet — and they threw in some money for education, for later.
sentences.zh: 被家乡的太空人队选中尤其甜蜜——而且他们还额外提供了一些钱用于日后的教育。

sentences.en: But Humphries wasn’t thinking about that.
sentences.zh: 但汉弗莱斯当时并没有想那么多。

sentences.en: He had one goal: to make the majors. So he went off to the Astros’ minor-league team in Martinsville, Virginia.
sentences.zh: 他只有一个目标：进入大联盟。于是他前往太空人队位于弗吉尼亚州马丁斯维尔的小联盟球队。

sentences.en: And then more teams in Kentucky, Louisiana, Florida, New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 然后是肯塔基州、路易斯安那州、佛罗里达州、新泽西州的更多球队。

sentences.en: But not, you may have noticed, Houston. He hit pretty well — but he hurt his wrist, and then his knee, and in 2009, at the ripe age of 27, Humphries quit baseball.
sentences.zh: 但你可能注意到了，没有休斯敦。他击球表现不错——但他伤了手腕，接着又伤了膝盖，在2009年，正值27岁的大好年华，汉弗莱斯退出了棒球界。

sentences.en: Now, only 11 percent of the kids who get drafted each year make the majors; but probably close to 100 percent of them think they will.
sentences.zh: 如今，每年被选中的孩子中只有11%能进入大联盟；但可能接近100%的人都觉得自己能进。

sentences.en: Humphries, even before he quit for good, started back in school, at a junior college in Texas.
sentences.zh: 汉弗莱斯甚至在彻底放弃之前，就已经在德克萨斯州的一所两年制专科学校重新开始上学了。

sentences.en: He wound up transferring to Columbia University, where he took a sociology course with a professor named Sudhir Venkatesh.
sentences.zh: 他最终转学到哥伦比亚大学，在那里他上了一门由苏迪尔·文卡特什（Sudhir Venkatesh）教授的社会学课程。

sentences.en: You may recognize that name. We wrote about his exploits in Freakonomics; as a grad student in Chicago, Venkatesh embedded himself with a crack gang, and got access to their financial records.
sentences.zh: 你可能认得这个名字。我们在《魔鬼经济学》中写过他的事迹；作为芝加哥大学的研究生，文卡特什曾深入一个贩毒帮派内部，并获得了他们的财务记录。

sentences.en: We wrote about him in SuperFreakonomics too: He did an extensive survey of street prostitutes.
sentences.zh: 我们在《超级魔鬼经济学》中也写过他：他对街头妓女进行过广泛的调查。

sentences.en: Guess what Venkatesh is studying these days?
sentences.zh: 你猜文卡特什最近在研究什么？

sentences.en: I’m interested in quitting for a number of reasons, not the least of which is that it’s hard for me to do it.
sentences.zh: 我之所以对放弃感兴趣有很多原因，其中很不重要的一点是，我自己很难做到这一点。

sentences.en: But I also think it’s just really, really hard the older you get, especially when you start identifying yourself with a job.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，随着年龄增长，这会变得非常非常难，尤其是当你开始把自我认同和工作绑定在一起的时候。

sentences.en: All right, so you actually looked in a fairly systematic, empirical way at baseball players.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以你实际上以一种相当系统、实证的方式研究了棒球运动员。

sentences.en: So, I actually never thought I would be interested in looking at baseball from the standpoint of a job, and one of my students, Justin Humphries, used to play baseball for the Houston Astros organization.
sentences.zh: 所以，我其实从未想过自己会对从一份工作的角度来看待棒球感兴趣，我的一个学生贾斯汀·汉弗莱斯过去曾在休斯敦太空人队组织里打过棒球。

sentences.en: And he was in my class. So, I was sitting in his classroom, I started thinking about all the issues that I had seen in independent baseball and affiliated baseball: guys living check-to-check, struggling with whether they should go back to school, family life, issues at home.
sentences.zh: 他当时在我的课上。所以，我坐在他的课堂上，我开始思考我在独立棒球和附属棒球中看到的所有问题：靠薪水度日的球员，纠结着是否应该重返校园，家庭生活，家里的种种问题。

sentences.en: And I thought if I could use some of the things that we were learning in class, talk to some of these guys, and find out whether the stories and things that I was seeing and hearing would be reflected in the numbers.
sentences.zh: 我想，如果我能运用我们在课堂上学到的一些东西，跟这些家伙聊聊，弄清楚我看到和听到的故事和事情是否会在数据中得到反映。

sentences.en: We followed a sample of the draft class of 2001, and so that’s about 10 years, and so we thought that would help us understand what happens to these folks.
sentences.zh: 我们追踪了2001届选秀的样本，时间大约是10年，所以我们认为这能帮我们了解这些人后来遭遇了什么。

sentences.en: Now, this doesn’t include the immigrants because when they came into the country and they didn’t go through the draft to play ball.
sentences.zh: 现在，这不包括移民，因为他们来到这个国家时并没有通过选秀来打球。

sentences.en: These are just the people who were out of high school or who were in college, and they were drafted by a major league team.
sentences.zh: 这些人只是那些高中毕业或上过大学，然后被大联盟球队选中的人。

sentences.en: I think one of the most curious things that we find is how much 10 years matter.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们发现的最奇怪的事情之一，就是这10年的影响有多大。

sentences.en: If you take two people who grew up in the same circumstances, let’s say one played baseball and one didn’t, the person who plays baseball is making about 40 percent less on average 10 years after they enter the game than the person who decides not to play baseball and who just wanted a regular career.
sentences.zh: 如果你找两个在相同环境下长大的年轻人，比如一个打棒球，另一个不打，在进入这个行业10年后，打棒球的人平均收入比那个决定不打棒球、只想要一份普通职业的人要少大约40%。

sentences.en: All right, so what kind of background was typical for the American-born players that you’re tracking?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么你所追踪的美国本土球员通常都有什么样的背景？

sentences.en: The average player probably looks like an upper-middle-class kid who comes out of college or comes out of high school.
sentences.zh: 普通球员看起来可能就像是一个中产阶级上层的孩子，大学毕业或高中毕业。

sentences.en: And when you follow an upper-middle-class kid for about seven to 10 years, they’re probably going to make higher than the median average income.
sentences.zh: 当你追踪一个中产阶级上层的孩子大约七到十年时，他们的收入可能会高于中位数平均水平。

sentences.en: They’re probably going to live in a neighborhood that’s relatively safe.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会住在相对安全的社区里。

sentences.en: They’re going to have a career. Now, when you take the counterpart among the pool that was drafted, that median kid, that kid looks likes he’s making about 20 to 24 thousand dollars a year, which is not a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 他们会拥有一份职业。现在，当你看看被选中的群体中的同类时，那个处于中位数的孩子，看起来他一年的收入大约在2万到2万4千美元之间，这可不是一笔大钱。

sentences.en: He’s working probably five to seven months playing baseball, and then struggling to find part-time work in the off-season.
sentences.zh: 他可能花五到七个月的时间打棒球，然后在休赛期艰难地寻找兼职工作。

sentences.en: Might be coaching, might be doing some training, might be working on a construction site.
sentences.zh: 可能是当教练，做点训练，或者在建筑工地干活。

sentences.en: Might be working in fast food. So, Sudhir, you went down to Camden not long ago, right?
sentences.zh: 可能在快餐店打工。所以，苏迪尔，你不久前去了卡姆登，对吧？

sentences.en: To talk to some of these ball players? Camden is in the Atlantic League.
sentences.zh: 去和其中一些棒球运动员聊聊？卡姆登在大西洋联盟。

sentences.en: That’s an independent league, meaning there’s no direct path to a big-league team.
sentences.zh: 那是一个独立联盟，意味着没有通往大联盟球队的直接道路。

sentences.en: A lot of the guys on a team like this have already been through the minor leagues and either topped out in talent or aged out, right?
sentences.zh: 像这样的球队里的很多队员都已经经历过小联盟，要么是天赋到头了，要么是年龄超龄了，对吧？

sentences.en: So they’re not really prepared to talk about it, except some.
sentences.zh: 所以他们其实并不太愿意谈论这个，除了极少数人。

sentences.en: Particularly this guy Noah Hall was a really, really interesting person because he actually was thinking that this may be the end.
sentences.zh: 特别是这个叫诺亚·霍尔（Noah Hall）的家伙，他是一个非常非常有趣的人，因为他其实在想这可能是他的终点。

sentences.en: It’s probably not happening, you know. It’s probably not happening, but I’m still going to, you know, prepare and everything the same way I would, regardless, you know?
sentences.zh: 可能不会发生了，你知道的。可能不会发生了，但无论如何，我还是会，你知道的，像往常一样做准备和做所有事情，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Because you never know. You still never know.
sentences.zh: 因为你永远不知道。你还是永远不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, in the back, the way back of my mind it’s still there, you know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在我脑海的最深处，它仍然在那里，你知道的。

sentences.en: I know, I feel like, trust me, I feel like sometimes hey, if I have a good start to this year, whatever happens you never know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我觉得，相信我，我觉得有时候嘿，如果我今年开局不错，不管发生什么，你永远不知道。

sentences.en: I could get picked up, and if I went off wherever I went, it could happen.
sentences.zh: 我可能会被选中，如果我去了我去的任何地方，事情可能会发生。

sentences.en: Noah is 34. Noah has been playing 16 seasons including this one.
sentences.zh: 诺亚34岁了。包括这一次在内，诺亚已经打了16个赛季。

sentences.en: When you look at him, you probably don’t think that he is a baseball player.
sentences.zh: 当你看着他时，你可能不会觉得他是个棒球运动员。

sentences.en: He looks like a running back. This is a guy who really looks like he’s never ever going to stop playing.
sentences.zh: 他看起来像个跑卫。这是一个看起来真的永远、永远不会停止打球的家伙。

sentences.en: Some guys just see the writing on the wall.
sentences.zh: 有些家伙只是看清了墙上的字（大势已趋）。

sentences.en: And I just try to ignore the writing on the wall.
sentences.zh: 而我只是试着不去理会墙上的字。

sentences.en: I don’t know; I don’t want to look back and say I didn’t give it everything I could.
sentences.zh: 我不知道；我不想回过头来说我没有付出我所能付出的一切。

sentences.en: I think I still, I could still play another five, 10 years, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我依然，我还能再打五、十年，我想。

sentences.en: So Noah’s from Northern California, and he was raised by his mom, a nurse.
sentences.zh: 所以诺亚来自北加州，他是被当护士的妈妈抚养长大的。

sentences.en: And Noah has a wife, Kelly — and they have a lovely son, Isaiah.
sentences.zh: 诺亚有一个妻子凯莉——他们还有一个可爱的儿子以赛亚。

sentences.en: And Kelly and Isaiah follow Noah around to whatever team he ends up playing for that season — and let me tell you he’s played on a lot of teams over the years.
sentences.zh: 凯莉和以赛亚跟着诺亚到处跑，无论他那个赛季效力于哪支球队——让我告诉你，这些年来他效力过很多球队。

sentences.en: After Noah’s practice, I had a chance to go out to dinner with the Hall family and get to know them a little bit.
sentences.zh: 诺亚训练结束后，我有机会和霍尔一家一起出去吃晚饭，并对他们有了更多的了解。

sentences.en: I’m the one who’s there like when he gets out and has a good game or when he has a bad game.
sentences.zh: 我是那个在他被淘汰或者打了一场好比赛或打了一场烂比赛时陪在身边的人。

sentences.en: I’m the one … I go through that kind of emotional roller coaster with him.
sentences.zh: 我就是那个……我和他一起经历那种情绪过山车的人。

sentences.en: So one of the strange things we found out when we spoke to baseball players is that they have their own language for quitting.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们和棒球运动员交谈时，我们发现的一件奇怪的事情是，他们有自己的一套关于放弃的语言。

sentences.en: They actually quit. They just don’t call it that.
sentences.zh: 他们其实是放弃了。他们只是不这么叫。

sentences.en: They don’t call it quitting. They don’t call it giving up.
sentences.zh: 他们不称之为放弃。他们不称之为认输。

sentences.en: But, they say, “You know what? I’m just going to shut it down for a while.” So, what does it mean to be a quitter as opposed to a “shutter downer?” Probably the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但是，他们会说，“你知道吗？我只是要暂时关闭它一段时间。”所以，作为一个“关机者”而不是一个“放弃者”意味着什么？可能是一回事。

sentences.en: It just sounds better when you say, “I’m just shutting down.’ You know, it’s like you’re not really doing it, but, you know, you are.
sentences.zh: 只是当你自我安慰说“我只是在关机”时，听起来好听一点。你懂的，就像你其实不是在认输，但是，你知道的，你其实就是。

sentences.en: Have you ever wanted to tell them, but you had to hold yourself back?
sentences.zh: 你有没有曾经想过告诉他们，但又不得不克制自己？

sentences.en: To shut it down? All the time. Oh yeah? Oh yeah, all the time.
sentences.zh: 去关闭它？一直想。哦，是吗？哦，是啊，一直都想。

sentences.en: Especially in the last couple of years. Yeah, especially in the last couple of years we’ve really … we’ve actually fought over it.
sentences.zh: 特别是在过去几年里。是的，特别是在过去几年里，我们真的……我们实际上为此吵过架。

sentences.en: Because it is, it’s so hard. Like I understand, being his wife and trying to be supportive.
sentences.zh: 因为确实，这太难了。就像我理解的那样，作为他的妻子，我努力去支持他。

sentences.en: I understand that it’s got to be really hard, because I do know how much he loves the game.
sentences.zh: 我明白这肯定非常难，因为我确实知道他有多么热爱这项比赛。

sentences.en: Wow, that’s particularly poignant in my view, because you know, because baseball’s one of those rare sports that because it doesn’t have a clock, no game is ever out of reach.
sentences.zh: 哇，在我看来这特别令人辛酸，因为你知道的，因为棒球是那种罕见的运动，由于它没有计时器，任何比赛都永远有追回的可能。

sentences.en: I mean, you could be behind a thousand runs in the bottom of the ninth and theoretically you can still come back and win.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在第九局下半你可能落后了一千分，但理论上你仍然可以卷土重来并赢得比赛。

sentences.en: So that’s part of the ethic of baseball is never, never, never quit.
sentences.zh: 所以棒球的精神之一就是永不、永不、永不放弃。

sentences.en: Quitting is not an option. Yeah, quitting is usually not an option.
sentences.zh: 放弃不是一个选项。是的，放弃通常不是一个选项。

sentences.en: But Justin is trying to make it easier on the players to quit and to make that transition.
sentences.zh: 但贾斯汀正在努力让球员更容易放弃并完成这种转型。

sentences.en: He’s been working on building an organization that could help players to get out of baseball when the time is right and to join that world that the rest of us live in.
sentences.zh: 他一直在致力于建立一个组织，帮助球员在合适的时机离开棒球界，并融入我们其他人生活的那个世界。

sentences.en: Well, when you’re 25, playing in independent ball, making less than $2,000 a month, living off your parents because you can’t financially sustain yourself like that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，当你25岁时，在独立联盟打球，每月挣不到2000美元，靠父母接济生活，因为你在经济上无法那样维持自己。

sentences.en: At some point you have to say, to look … with no degree.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，你必须对自己说，看看……而且还没有学位。

sentences.en: I had less than an associates degree at that point.
sentences.zh: 那时我连副学士学位都不到。

sentences.en: So, at some point, you have to tell yourself, “I can’t do this to myself.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某个时刻，你必须对自己说：“我不能这样对折磨自己。

sentences.en: I can’t do this to my parents. And I can’t continue when I know that they’re untapped potential to do other things.” So Justin Humphries stared right into the dark heart of his sunk costs, all those years he spent pursuing his dream – and he made the big quit.
sentences.zh: 我不能这样对待我的父母。当我知道自己还有去做其他事情的未开发潜力时，我不能再继续下去了。”于是贾斯汀·汉弗莱斯直面了他沉没成本的黑暗核心，那些他用来追求梦想的岁月——然后他来了个彻底的大放弃。

sentences.en: We’ll hear more from Sudhir Venkatesh later in the show.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目稍后会听到更多来自苏迪尔·文卡特什的讲述。

sentences.en: In a moment, we’ll tell you what my number-crunching Freakonomics co-author Steve Levitt has in common with a bunch of abs-crunching Navy SEALs.
sentences.zh: 稍后，我们将告诉你我的《魔鬼经济学》合著者、疯狂计算数字的史密·莱维特（Steve Levitt）和一群疯狂锻炼腹肌的海豹突击队员有什么共同点。

sentences.en: So for ballplayers like Justin Humphries and Noah Hall, quitting their athletic dream is a long, painful process.
sentences.zh: 所以对于像贾斯汀·汉弗莱斯和诺亚 Hall 这样的棒球运动员来说，放弃他们的运动梦想是一个漫长而痛苦的过程。

sentences.en: Steve Levitt — he’s my Freakonomics friend and co-author, an economist at the University of Chicago — he advocates quitting fast.
sentences.zh: 史密·莱维特——他是我的魔鬼经济学好友兼合著者，芝加哥大学的经济学家——他主张快速放弃。

sentences.en: I try to talk my grad students into quitting all the time.
sentences.zh: 我一直试图劝说我的研究生放弃。

sentences.en: Quitting grad school? Quitting grad school, yeah.
sentences.zh: 放弃读研？放弃读研，是的。

sentences.en: A lot of people — you make choices without a lot of information and then you get new information.
sentences.zh: 很多人——你在没有获得充足信息的情况下做出选择，然后你获得了新的信息。

sentences.en: And quitting is often the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 而放弃往往是正确的做法。

sentences.en: I try to talk my kids into quitting soccer, baseball if they’re not good at it.
sentences.zh: 我试图劝说我的孩子们放弃足球、棒球，如果他们不擅长的话。

sentences.en: I mean, I’ve never had any shame in quitting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我从来不为放弃感到羞耻。

sentences.en: I’ve quit economic theory, I quit macroeconomics.
sentences.zh: 我放弃了经济学理论，我放弃了宏观经济学。

sentences.en: I’ve pretty much quit everything that I’m bad at.
sentences.zh: 我基本上放弃了我所有不擅长的东西。

sentences.en: You do have this mantra: Fail fast. Fail quickly, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 你确实有这样一个座右铭：快速失败。迅速失败，对，没错。

sentences.en: So if I were to say one of the single most important explanations for how I managed to succeed against all odds in the field of economics, it was by being a quitter.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我要说我在经济学领域历经重重困难却能成功的最大原因之一，那就是我是一个放弃者。

sentences.en: That ever since the beginning, my mantra has been, “Fail quickly.” If I started with a hundred ideas, I’m lucky if two or three of those ideas will ever turn into academic papers.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，我的座右铭就是，“迅速失败。”如果我有一百个想法，能有两三个想法最终变成学术论文我就很幸运了。

sentences.en: One of my great skills as an economist has been to recognize the need to fail quickly and the willingness to jettison a project as soon as I realize it’s likely to fail.
sentences.zh: 作为一名经济学家，我伟大的技能之一就是认识到迅速失败的必要性，并且一旦我意识到一个项目很可能会失败时，就果断抛弃它的意愿。

sentences.en: Getting talked into quitting grad school by your 155-pound professor is one thing.
sentences.zh: 被你那个155磅重的教授说服放弃读研是一回事。

sentences.en: How about a Navy SEAL instructor? So Hell Week is considered to be the hardest week of the hardest military training in the world.
sentences.zh: 海豹突击队教官怎么样？所以地狱周被认为是世界上最艰难的军事训练中最艰难的一周。

sentences.en: That’s Eric Greitens. He got a Ph. D. in politics from Oxford and then joined the Navy SEALS.
sentences.zh: 那是埃里克·格雷滕斯（Eric Greitens）。他在牛津获得政治学博士学位，然后加入了海豹突击队。

sentences.en: He fought in Iraq, Afghanistan, and elsewhere, and has now has written a book called The Heart and the Fist: The Education of a Humanitarian, the Making of a Navy SEAL.
sentences.zh: 他在伊拉克、阿富汗和其他地方战斗过，现在写了一本名为《心与拳：一个人道主义者的教育，一个海豹突击队员的炼成》（The Heart and the Fist: The Education of a Humanitarian, the Making of a Navy SEAL）的书。

sentences.en: Here’s how Greitens remembers Hell Week.
sentences.zh: 格雷滕斯是这样回忆地狱周的。

sentences.en: It is a week of continuous military training during which most classes sleep for a total of two to five hours over the course of the entire week.
sentences.zh: 那是连续一周的军事训练，在此期间，大多数学员在整个星期的总睡眠时间只有两到五个小时。

sentences.en: During Hell Week they have you running for miles in soft sand on the beach, doing two-mile ocean swims, running the obstacle course, they put you on small teams and ask you to land small rubber boats on jagged rocks in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 在地狱周期间，他们让你在海滩的软沙里跑好几英里，进行两英里的海洋游泳，跑障碍训练场，他们把你分成小组，要求你在半夜将小型橡皮艇登陆在布满锯齿状岩石的海岸上。

sentences.en: There are all of these tests which are designed to push people to their physical, mental and emotional limit.
sentences.zh: 有所有这些旨在将人们推向身体、精神和情感极限的测试。

sentences.en: Hell Week is a useful way for the Navy to determine who’s fit to be a SEAL, the kind of person you’d want to send to get Osama Bin Laden.
sentences.zh: 地狱周是海军确定谁适合成为海豹突击队队员的一种有用方法，也就是那种你会想要派去干掉本·拉登的人。

sentences.en: Greitens says the instructors hover over you, taunting you, practically begging you to quit.
sentences.zh: 格雷滕斯说，教官们在你身边盘旋，嘲讽你，几乎是在求你放弃。

sentences.en: And the vast majority would quit before it was over.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数人会在结束前放弃。

sentences.en: That’s the point. You’ll hear the instructors come out with their bullhorns and they’d say, “That’s right, gentlemen, this is only the beginning of the second night.” And what they did then was the instructors took us out and they lined us up on the beach and they had us watch as the sun was setting.
sentences.zh: 这就是重点。你会听到教官拿着大喇叭出来说：“没错，先生们，这只是第二天晚上的开始。”他们接下来做的是，教官把我们带出去，让我们在海滩上排成一列，让我们看着太阳落山。

sentences.en: And as the sun was setting the instructors started to get inside people’s minds and said, “Tonight is going to be the hardest and the coldest and the toughest night of your lives.” And they’d come over their bullhorns and they’d say, “The week just gets colder and tougher and worse and you’re only at the beginning.” And they really started to get inside people’s minds.
sentences.zh: 当太阳落山时，教官们开始攻心，说道：“今晚将是你们一生中最寒冷、最严酷、最艰难的一夜。”他们会通过大喇叭说：“这一周只会越来越冷、越来越难、越来越糟，而你们才刚刚开始。”他们真的开始钻进人们的心里。

sentences.en: And I can remember the instructor saying at one point, “If anybody quits right now, we’ll give you a hot coffee and doughnuts.” Everybody was freezing, so they set up this little incentive over there if you want to go over and ring the bell you can quit and they’ll give you hot coffee and doughnuts.
sentences.zh: 我记得教官有一次说：“如果现在有人放弃，我们会给你一杯热咖啡和甜甜圈。”每个人都在挨冻，所以他们在那里设置了这样一个微小的激励，如果你想过去摇铃，你就可以放弃，他们会给你热咖啡和甜甜圈。

sentences.en: And the whole idea is that the instructors really encourage, they want everyone to succeed, but if people are going to quit, they want to encourage them to quit.
sentences.zh: 整个理念是，教官们真的很鼓励，他们希望每个人都成功，但如果人们要放弃，他们希望鼓励他们放弃。

sentences.en: When you quit by the bell, you ring it three times.
sentences.zh: 当你通过摇铃来放弃时，你要摇三下。

sentences.en: This tells everyone in earshot that you’re done.
sentences.zh: 这会告诉听力范围内的所有人你已经结束了。

sentences.en: Greitens says that there are two kinds of quitters.
sentences.zh: 格雷滕斯说，有两种放弃者。

sentences.en: The ones who make excuses and the ones who are honest with themselves.
sentences.zh: 那些找借口的人和对自己诚实的人。

sentences.en: I don’t think many people want to say to themselves that they’ve quit.
sentences.zh: 我想没多少人愿意对自己说他们放弃了。

sentences.en: At the same time, we’ve all failed in our lives, we’ve all failed at different things in different ways and I think there’s a lot to be said about facing that failure squarely.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们都在生活中失败过，我们在不同的事情上以不同的方式失败过，我认为正视这种失败大有可为。

sentences.en: And the people who I know, who were able to admit, you know, “This isn’t right for me at this time and I went over and I decided to quit, I decided to ring the bell,” they’re really able to move on from their experience.
sentences.zh: 而我认识的那些能够承认的人，你知道，“这在目前不适合我，我走了过去，决定放弃，我决定摇铃，”他们真的能够从他们的经历中走出来。

sentences.en: And I do find that there’s only shame in it if you feel shame.
sentences.zh: 我确实发现，只有当你感到羞耻时，它才会有羞耻感。

sentences.en: So what would you say if I told you there’s evidence that quitting is good for you?
sentences.zh: 那么如果我告诉你，有证据表明放弃对你有好处，你会怎么想？

sentences.en: Physiologically and psychologically good for you?
sentences.zh: 在生理和心理上对你都有好处？

sentences.en: People who are better able to let go when they experience unattainable goals, they have the experience, for example, less depressive symptoms, less negative affect over time.
sentences.zh: 那些在经历无法企及的目标时能够更好地放手的人，例如，他们的抑郁症状更少，随着时间的推移消极情绪更少。

sentences.en: They also have lower cortisol levels, and they have lower levels of systemic inflammation which is a marker of immune functioning.
sentences.zh: 他们的皮质醇水平也更低，系统性炎症水平也更低，这是免疫功能的标志。

sentences.en: And they develop fewer physical health problems over time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他们发展的身体健康问题也更少。

sentences.en: That’s Carsten Wrosch — no relation to Robert Reich.
sentences.zh: 那是卡斯滕·弗罗斯奇（Carsten Wrosch）——跟罗伯特·赖克没有任何关系。

sentences.en: Wrosch is a psychology professor at Concordia University in Montreal.
sentences.zh: 弗罗斯奇是蒙特利尔康考迪亚大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: In a study of 90 adolescents, he and a colleague found that being able to abandon goals that are essentially unattainable is good for your health.
sentences.zh: 在一项针对90名青少年的研究中，他和一位同事发现，能够放弃那些本质上无法实现的目标对你的健康有益。

sentences.en: Now, you have to ask yourself — what’s unattainable and what’s not?
sentences.zh: 现在，你必须问问自己——什么能实现，什么不能？

sentences.en: When Justin Humphries was 18 years old, the major leagues seemed pretty attainable.
sentences.zh: 当贾斯汀·汉弗莱斯18岁时，大联盟似乎还是相当可以企及的。

sentences.en: By 25? Not so much. If I were put through Hell Week?
sentences.zh: 到了25岁？就没那么容易了。如果让我经历地狱周？

sentences.en: Unattainable. According to Wrosch, each of us encounters an unattainable goal about once a year.
sentences.zh: 无法企及。根据弗罗斯奇的说法，我们每个人大约一年会遇到一次无法企及的目标。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, nobody’s walking around with a big neon sign urging us to quit.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，没有人带着亮眼的霓虹灯走来敦促我们放弃。

sentences.en: This is a puzzle and we need your help in solving it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个谜，我们需要你的帮助来解开它。

sentences.en: If persistence is a virtue, generally, how is a person to know when he or she under which circumstances he or she should quit or disengage?
sentences.zh: 如果坚持通常是一种美德，一个人如何才能知道在何时、在什么情况下他或她应该放弃或退出？

sentences.en: Yeah, that’s I would say the one-million-dollar question.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这可以说是价值百万美元的问题。

sentences.en: When to struggle and when to quit. I don’t think it’s a general answer to this question.
sentences.zh: 何时苦撑，何时放弃。我认为这个问题没有一个普遍的答案。

sentences.en: However, people can make two different mistakes in the regulation of their life.
sentences.zh: 然而，人们在生活调节中会犯两种不同的错误。

sentences.en: They can quit too early when they should have persisted or they can quit too late.
sentences.zh: 他们可能在应该坚持的时候放弃得太早，或者他们放弃得太晚。

sentences.en: OK. No offense, Professor Wrosch but that’s not very helpful.
sentences.zh: 好吧。无意冒犯，弗罗斯奇教授，但这并没有什么帮助。

sentences.en: Sometimes you quit too early when you should have persisted and sometimes you persist too long when you should have quit?
sentences.zh: 有时你在应该坚持的时候放弃得太早，而有时你在应该放弃的时候坚持得太久？

sentences.en: Really, that’s all you’ve got? Really, that’s all he’s got.
sentences.zh: 真的，这就是你全部的见解？真的，这就是他全部的见解。

sentences.en: Which shows, if nothing else, what a true dilemma this is — to quit or not to quit.
sentences.zh: 这至少表明了，放弃还是不放弃，这是一个多么真实的两难境地。

sentences.en: Let me ask you this, are you much of a quitter?
sentences.zh: 让我问你这个，你是个爱放弃的人吗？

sentences.en: I am bad at quitting. I really have a difficult time.
sentences.zh: 我很不擅长放弃。我真的觉得很困难。

sentences.en: I try to persist as much as possible. Maybe that’s why this phenomenon is so interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 我尽量去坚持。也许这就是这个现象对我来说如此有趣的原因吧。

sentences.en: Well maybe I can help you. Why don’t you tell me something that you’re involved in that you think is a goal that may be unattainable and I’ll try to talk you into quitting.
sentences.zh: 也许我能帮到你。你为什么不跟我说说你正在参与的一件你认为是无法实现的目标的事情，我会试着说服你放弃。

sentences.en: Well, at this point I can’t think about something that is unattainable right now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，此时此刻我想不出有什么是现在无法实现的。

sentences.en: But these things they pop up over time.
sentences.zh: 但这些事情随着时间推移会自己冒出来。

sentences.en: Do you smoke by chance? Yeah, actually I’m a smoker.
sentences.zh: 你抽烟吗？对，其实我是个烟民。

sentences.en: Do you want to quit smoking? Well, yeah, on some level but on a different level I enjoy it very much.
sentences.zh: 你想戒烟吗？嗯，是的，在某种程度上想，但在另一方面我很享受它。

sentences.en: This conversation went on for a while. I’ll spare you the details.
sentences.zh: 这段对话持续了一段时间。我省去了细节。

sentences.en: Let me say this: Either I’m incredibly unpersuasive or Carsten Wrosch really, really doesn’t want to quit smoking.
sentences.zh: 我要这么说：要么是我极其缺乏说服力，要么是卡斯滕·弗罗斯奇真的、真的不想戒烟。

sentences.en: Maybe both. He says he wants to quit, but he doesn’t really sound like it.
sentences.zh: 也许两者皆有。他说他想戒烟，但他听起来并不真心想戒。

sentences.en: It’s like an O. Henry story: The professor of quitting who can’t quit smoking.
sentences.zh: 这就像欧·亨利的小说：戒烟教授却戒不掉烟。

sentences.en: You can empathize, can’t you? I can empathize.
sentences.zh: 你能感同身受，对吧？我能感同身受。

sentences.en: There’s something you really want to quit, you know you’ll be healthier for it, but you can’t.
sentences.zh: 有些事情你真的很想放弃，你知道为了它你会更健康，但你就是做不到。

sentences.en: You try and you try and you try but you just can’t.
sentences.zh: 你尝试、尝试、再尝试，但就是做不到。

sentences.en: Until one day, finally, you wake up and you have this vision of what your life would be without that thing in it — and it’s not so terrible!
sentences.zh: 直到有一天，终于，你醒来，脑海中浮现出这样一幅画面：如果没有那个东西在你的生活中，你的生活会是什么样——而它其实并没有那么糟糕！

sentences.en: That’s how my first quit happened.
sentences.zh: 我的第一次放弃就是那样发生的。

sentences.en: Yep, that’s my old band. We were called The Right Profile.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是我的老乐队。我们叫The Right Profile。

sentences.en: Started in college, down in North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 在大学时开始的，在北卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: There were four of us. We were pretty bad at first.
sentences.zh: 我们有四个人。一开始我们挺烂的。

sentences.en: But we took it seriously, kept at it.
sentences.zh: 但我们很认真，一直坚持下去。

sentences.en: And that’s how I sound when I sing. We worked hard at it because it was incredibly fun but also because it was our dream.
sentences.zh: 这就是我唱歌时的声音。我们为此努力工作，因为这令人难以置信的有趣，也因为这是我们的梦想。

sentences.en: I mean, c’mon, who doesn’t dream at some point of being a rock star?
sentences.zh: 拜托，谁在某个时刻不曾梦想过成为摇滚明星呢？

sentences.en: All right, so Jon, when you hear that song which you didn’t play on this recording but you played this song, I don’t know many times you ended up playing this song in your life.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以乔恩，当你听到这首歌时——你在这段录音里没有弹奏它，但你弹过这歌，我不知道你这辈子最终弹过这首歌多少次。

sentences.en: Probably at least 50 times. That’s Jon Wurster. (We called him Chester but his actual name is Jon.) He was our drummer — awesome drummer.
sentences.zh: 可能至少50次。那是乔恩·伍斯特（Jon Wurster）。（我们叫他切斯特，但他真名叫乔恩。）他是我们的鼓手——超棒的鼓手。

sentences.en: You might know his name – he went on to play with Superchunk for years.
sentences.zh: 你可能知道他的名字——他后来为Superchunk乐队演奏了好多年。

sentences.en: He still plays with them, and with the Mountain Goats too.
sentences.zh: 他现在仍然和他们一起演奏，也和The Mountain Goats一起演奏。

sentences.en: The other guys in the band were Jeff Foster and Tim Fleming.
sentences.zh: 乐队的其他成员是杰夫·福斯特（Jeff Foster）和蒂姆·弗莱明（Tim Fleming）。

sentences.en: We played all over the place. We made demo tapes, released a single.
sentences.zh: 我们到处演出。我们制作了样带，发行了一张单曲。

sentences.en: Got a management team in New York City, the same guys who managed the Replacements and the Del Fuegos, which were bands that we loved.
sentences.zh: 我们在纽约市找到了一个管理团队，就是管理过Replacements和Del Fuegos乐队的那些人，那是我们热爱的乐队。

sentences.en: The managers brought us up to New York to play for the major record labels.
sentences.zh: 经纪人们把我们带到纽约去为各大唱片公司演出。

sentences.en: Two months later, I remember going to the CBGB’s in New York to play there a showcase show for some labels, one of which was Arista and I remember just in this total dive, CBGB’s, there was a table and on the table was a card that said “Reserved for Clive Davis.” Do you remember going up to their office on that trip?
sentences.zh: 两个月后，我记得去纽约的CBGB酒吧为一些唱片公司在那里表演一场展示演出，其中一家是Arista，我记得就在这个绝对破烂的地方CBGB，有一张桌子上有一张卡片，上面写着“克里夫·戴维斯（Clive Davis）预留”。你还记得那次旅行中去过他们的办公室吗？

sentences.en: Do you remember when he had Aretha on the phone briefly to tell us to sign with Arista?
sentences.zh: 你还记得他当时简短地让Aretha（Franklin）通电话告诉我们要签约Arista吗？

sentences.en: Yes. I remember when some people … when everybody kind of walked away we would go and look through people’s Rolodexes to find the personal numbers of Carly Simon and somebody else.
sentences.zh: 记得。我记得当某些人……当大家差不多都离开时，我们会去翻看别人的 Rolodex（旋转名片座），寻找卡莉·西蒙（Carly Simon）和其他人的私人号码。

sentences.en: We never used them but we just thought that was hilarious just to like thumb through this Rolodex and find her number.
sentences.zh: 我们从没用过它们，但我们只是觉得翻看这个 Rolodex 并找到她的号码非常搞笑。

sentences.en: So, it’s true: Clive Davis, the music-industry giant, signed us to Arista Records.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是真的：音乐产业巨头克里夫·戴维斯将我们签到了Arista唱片公司。

sentences.en: It was incredibly exciting. But also weird.
sentences.zh: 这令人难以置信地兴奋。但也很诡异。

sentences.en: We were this little indie, half-punky half-country band, used to doing things the way we did them, and now we moved to New York.
sentences.zh: 我们只是这个独立的小乐队，一半朋克一半乡村，习惯了用我们自己的方式做事，而现在我们搬到了纽约。

sentences.en: It was hard. Maybe we were just a bad fit with Arista.
sentences.zh: 这很难。也许我们跟Arista本来就不搭。

sentences.en: They wanted pop hits; we didn’t seem to have them.
sentences.zh: 他们想要流行金曲；而我们似乎没有。

sentences.en: The other thing is: I wasn’t sure I wanted to be a rock star anymore.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是：我不再确定自己是否还想当摇滚明星了。

sentences.en: As bands go, we were pretty straight-laced.
sentences.zh: 就乐队而言，我们相当循规蹈矩。

sentences.en: No drugs, not much drinking. But the whole lifestyle, especially as we got a little bit more successful and started hanging around with bigger bands — it became less attractive.
sentences.zh: 没有毒品，不怎么喝酒。但整个生活方式，尤其是当我们变得更成功一点、开始和更大的乐队混在一起时——它变得不那么吸引人了。

sentences.en: The idea of wanting to be famous — which seemed fun at first — began to feel unsavory, unhealthy.
sentences.zh: 渴望成名的想法——起初看起来很有趣——开始变得令人反感、不健康。

sentences.en: For six years, this was all I wanted. But one night I was sitting in a hotel room in Memphis, working on some lyrics in my notebook.
sentences.zh: 整整六年，这就是我想要的全部。但一天晚上，我在孟菲斯的某个酒店房间里，在笔记本上琢磨着一些歌词。

sentences.en: And I found myself writing the words, “What do I want?” I thought about it.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己写下了这样几个字：“我到底想要什么？”我陷入了沉思。

sentences.en: I didn’t really know anymore. And then, I wrote “Not this.” A couple weeks later, I quit the band.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道了。然后，我写下：“不是这个。”几个星期后，我退出了乐队。

sentences.en: We were playing some songs and we could just tell you were kind of moody and maybe something was wrong but we knew what was wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在弹奏一些歌曲，我们能看出你有点情绪化，也许有什么不对劲，但我们知道是什么不对劲。

sentences.en: We knew that this might be where it parts soon, we just kind of felt that.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这可能很快就是分道扬镳的时候了，我们多少能感觉到那种氛围。

sentences.en: We played something and I remember Jeff saying to you,”What’s wrong?” or “What’s your problem?” I don’t know exactly what you said but I remember something to the effect of, “I don’t think I want to do this anymore.” The hardest part was that being in the band wasn’t just what I did — it was what I was.
sentences.zh: 我们弹奏了一些东西，我记得杰夫对你说，“你怎么了？”或者“你有什么毛病？”我不记得你具体说了什么，但我记得大意是，“我觉得我不想再做这个了。”最难的部分是，身处乐队不仅是我在做的事——它就是我是谁。

sentences.en: Like Justin Humphries and the other ballplayers — baseball isn’t just a thing you do; it’s your identity.
sentences.zh: 就像贾斯汀·汉弗莱斯和其他棒球运动员一样——棒球不仅仅是你做的一件事；它是你的身份。

sentences.en: I’ll be honest with you, it was tough. I grieved; I mourned; and I had to start over, as a writer.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这很难。我感到悲伤；我感到哀悼；我不得不作为一名作家重新开始。

sentences.en: At that point, I didn’t know much about economics.
sentences.zh: 在那时，我对经济学知之甚少。

sentences.en: I’d never heard of the sunk-cost fallacy.
sentences.zh: 我从未听说过沉没成本谬误。

sentences.en: But by quitting something I’d put years of work into, that’s what I was fighting against.
sentences.zh: 但通过放弃一件我投入了多年心血的事情，这正是我当时在与之抗争的事情。

sentences.en: One of the most common examples is the Vietnam War because it was often said that we’ve invested too much to quit.
sentences.zh: 最常见的例子之一就是越南战争，因为人们经常说我们已经投入了太多，不能放弃。

sentences.en: Well, it’s not a good idea to continue to invest if you feel it’s a losing course of action.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你觉得这是一条注定失败的行动路线，继续投入并不是一个好大主意。

sentences.en: That’s Hal Arkes, he’s a psychology professor at Ohio State University.
sentences.zh: 那是哈尔·阿克斯（Hal Arkes），他是俄亥俄州立大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: A “sunk cost” is just what it sounds like: time or money you’ve already spent.
sentences.zh: “沉没成本”就像听起来那样：你已经花掉的时间或金钱。

sentences.en: The sunk-cost fallacy is when you tell yourself that you can’t quit because of all that time or money you spent.
sentences.zh: 沉没成本谬误是指你告诉自己你不能放弃，因为你已经花了那么多时间和金钱。

sentences.en: We shouldn’t fall for this fallacy, but we do it all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该陷入这个谬误，但我们一直在这样做。

sentences.en: Arkes and a colleague learned something that makes falling for the sunk-cost fallacy even more embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 阿克斯和一位同事发现了一件事，这让陷入沉没成本谬误变得更加尴尬。

sentences.en: It turns out that children don’t fall for it — or even animals.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，小孩子们不会陷入这种谬误——甚至动物也不会。

sentences.en: Your dog is not going to have any rules like “Oh, I spent a lot of time at that location waiting for him to feed me, and I wouldn’t want to waste all that time, so I’ll go back there and wait even though it wasn’t very successful.” Now, humans have these other things that get in the way.
sentences.zh: 你的狗才不会有什么规矩，比如“哦，我在那个地方花了很多时间等他喂我，我可不想浪费所有这些时间，所以我还要回到那里去等，尽管那次并不怎么成功。”现在，人类身上有其他一些东西碍事。

sentences.en: What gets in the way? Apparently we take a rule we learn growing up — to not be wasteful — and over-apply it.
sentences.zh: 是什么在碍事？显然，我们把成长过程中学到的一个规则——不要浪费——给过度应用了。

sentences.en: Well, there’s that chance that what we’re working on actually can be rescued, can be resuscitated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们正在做的事情实际上还有可能被拯救、被抢救回来，这种可能性是存在的。

sentences.en: Making the distinction and trying to decide whether this is a truly lost cause or not, I recognize is a difficult decision sometimes because it’s not one of these things where it’s clearly one or the other.
sentences.zh: 做出区分并试图决定这是否真的是一个无药可救的事业，我承认有时这是一个艰难的决定，因为它不是那种黑白分明的事情。

sentences.en: But after enough negative feedback, it should be more clear then.
sentences.zh: 但在经历了足够的负面反馈之后，那时应该就更清晰了。

sentences.en: I guess with my band, I’d finally had enough negative feedback to quit.
sentences.zh: 我想对于我的乐队来说，我终于收到了足够多的负面反馈，于是我退出了。

sentences.en: I’ll tell you the truth, some of the feedback, I still miss.
sentences.zh: 说实话，有些反馈，我至今仍然怀念。

sentences.en: It was insanely fun. And part of me still wishes I’d stuck it out, at least to finish that first record for Arista.
sentences.zh: 那是疯狂的有趣。而且我的一部分仍然希望我能坚持下去，至少完成给Arista的第一张唱片。

sentences.en: But the bottom line? I’m so glad I quit.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的是什么？我很高兴我退出了。

sentences.en: For me, it was the right move. Much as I miss music sometimes, the upside of quitting for me meant I got to lead a life more like the one that I envisioned.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是正确的举动。尽管有时我怀念音乐，但放弃带来的好处意味着我能够过上更接近我所设想的那种生活。

sentences.en: Coming up: Remember Allie — the high-end escort from the start of the show?
sentences.zh: 接下来：还记得艾莉吗——节目刚开始时那个高端伴游？

sentences.en: Well, she’s back — and quitting again.
sentences.zh: 好吧，她又回来了——而且再次退出了。

sentences.en: You remember Allie? The Texas woman who quit computer programming to become a high-end escort?
sentences.zh: 你还记得艾莉吗？那个辞去程序员工作成为高端伴游的德克萨斯女人？

sentences.en: Sure you do. At her peak, she was earning about $300,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 你当然记得。在她最红的时候，她一年大约能赚30万美元。

sentences.en: Now, Allie are you still working as an escort?
sentences.zh: 那么，艾莉，你还在当伴游吗？

sentences.en: No, I decided to get out of the escort business.
sentences.zh: 不，我决定退出伴游行业了。

sentences.en: You know, it was wonderful to me. I enjoyed it, I made a lot of money but I don’t regret quitting, either, again.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这对我很棒。我很享受，我赚了很多钱，但对于再次选择放弃，我同样毫不后悔。

sentences.en: But we talk about opportunity cost, and when I went into the escort business I wasn’t dating anybody, I just really wanted to enjoy life and be free and that’s what I did.
sentences.zh: 但我们讨论机会成本，当我进入伴游行业时，我没有在跟任何人谈恋爱，我只是真的很想享受生活、获得自由，而我也确实做到了。

sentences.en: But you know, I met somebody and we decided together that, you now, that we wanted a lifestyle that didn’t include prostitution.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，我遇到了某个人，我们共同决定，你知道的，我们想要一种不包含性交易的生活方式。

sentences.en: So, I let it go. And besides enjoying life and traveling and spending time with your companion, what else have you been doing?
sentences.zh: 所以，我放手了。除了享受生活、旅行和与伴侣共度时光，你还在做什么？

sentences.en: I went to school and studied economics, but you know, mostly I’m enjoying life.
sentences.zh: 我去上学并学习了经济学，但你知道的，主要还是在享受生活。

sentences.en: You know? All right, so I realize that Allie isn’t your typical prostitute.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？好吧，所以我意识到艾莉并不是那种典型的性工作者。

sentences.en: I mean, first of all, she made a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，首先，她赚了很多大钱。

sentences.en: On top of that, she went back to school to study economics!
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，她回去上学研究经济学了！

sentences.en: She really gets opportunity cost, so much so that, when the time was right, she quit being a prostitute.
sentences.zh: 她真的懂机会成本，以至于当时机成熟时，她就不干妓女了。

sentences.en: Sudhir Venkatesh, the sociologist who talked to fading baseball players for us, he’s also been asking prostitutes about quitting.
sentences.zh: 苏迪尔·文卡特什，那个为我们采访过走下坡路的棒球运动员的社会学家，他也一直在问妓女们关于退出的事。

sentences.en: But first, I asked him about something he recently quit.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我问了他关于他最近退出的一件事。

sentences.en: I quit an administrative job that I had at my university for a couple of years and actually probably should have quit after a couple days.
sentences.zh: 我辞去了大学里做了几年的行政工作，其实可能在干了几天后就该辞职了。

sentences.en: Why’d you quit, finally?
sentences.zh: 你为什么最终辞职了？

sentences.en: Well, I think I quit because I realized that I was no good at the job.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我辞职是因为我意识到我根本不适合那份工作。

sentences.en: You know, luckily I have a job as a professor, and so I’m not in the ranks of the unemployed like so many people who sometimes quit jobs that they don’t like.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，幸运的是我有一份教授的工作，所以我并不像许多偶尔辞掉不喜欢的工作的人那样沦为失业大军。

sentences.en: So I’m back to doing research, which I love.
sentences.zh: 所以我又回去做我热爱的研究了。

sentences.en: You heard me talking to Allie, who kind of falls into that rare category.
sentences.zh: 你听到我和艾莉的谈话了，她有点属于那种罕见的类别。

sentences.en: She’s someone who did very, very well and decided to, if not cash out necessarily, at least to stop.
sentences.zh: 她是一个干得非常非常出色，并决定哪怕不算是现金套现，至少也选择金盆洗手的人。

sentences.en: But I understand that you talked to some people, sex workers, one named Maxine I believe, who doesn’t see that as the way to go.
sentences.zh: 但我听说你和一些人交谈过，性工作者，其中一个叫麦克辛（Maxine），我相信她并不认为那是唯一的出路。

sentences.en: So talk to me a little bit about Maxine and her attitude toward quitting.
sentences.zh: 所以跟我聊聊麦克辛以及她对退出的态度。

sentences.en: I should say that we’re not using the real names of the women that we’re interviewed here, but Maxine, as we’re calling her, is a really curious person because she really goes against a lot of the stereotypes that we have about women in sex work.
sentences.zh: 我应该说明，我们在这里采访的女性并没有使用真实姓名，但我们称她为麦克辛的这个人非常引人注目，因为她真的违背了我们对性工作女性的很多刻板印象。

sentences.en: She’s been working as a sex worker for 22 years.
sentences.zh: 她做性工作已经22年了。

sentences.en: She laughs as she says, you know, I don’t know if I’m ever going to quit.
sentences.zh: 她笑着说，你知道的，我不知道自己会不会退出。

sentences.en: You know, I never think about retiring. I know many workers who are in their 50s, 60s, I met one in her early 70s who is still working.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我从来没想过退休。我认识很多50多岁、60多岁的从业者，我还遇到过一个70岁出头仍然在工作的人。

sentences.en: And in our current society with the tearing down of our infrastructures and our social security nets, all of us are going to be working for a long time.
sentences.zh: 而在我们这个基础设施和社会保障网正被拆解的现代社会里，我们所有人都将不得不工作很长很长时间。

sentences.en: All right, so there are those prostitutes who do quit.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以确实有那些选择不干了的性工作者。

sentences.en: And I just wonder, you know, how does that happen?
sentences.zh: 我就在想，你知道，这到底是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: If you want to go from sex work into the legitimate labor market, how do you go about, for instance, putting together a resume?
sentences.zh: 如果你想从性工作转入合法的劳动市场，比方说，你怎么着手去写一份简历呢？

sentences.en: Right, imagine you’ve been a sex worker for a year, two years, three years, five years, and you have to account for that time, you have to account for what you’ve done.
sentences.zh: 对吧，想象一下你当了一年、两年、三年、五年的性工作者，你必须交代这段时间，你必须交代你做过什么。

sentences.en: Crystal Deboise is the co-director of the Sex Workers Project at the Urban Justice Center in New York City, and actually one of the services the center provides, that Crystal helps sex workers with, is getting their resumes ready.
sentences.zh: Crystal Deboise 是纽约城市正义中心性工作者项目的联合负责人，事实上，该中心提供的服务之一、也就是 Crystal 帮助性工作者做的事情，就是帮他们准备简历。

sentences.en: So it becomes a creative endeavor. So we dig deep, and I say, well, what have you done?
sentences.zh: 所以这变成了一项富有创造力的工作。所以我们要深入挖掘，然后我说，嗯，你都做过什么？

sentences.en: Somebody might say, well I used to wash cars with my uncle on the weekends, and they’ll say, “Oh no that wasn’t a job, that was just a thing that I did.” And I was like, “No, we’re going to make that sound like you worked, you know, that it’s a job.
sentences.zh: 有人可能会说，嗯，我周末跟我叔叔一起洗过车，他们会说，“哦不，那可不算工作，那只是我顺手干的一件事。”而我会说，“不，我们要把它说得像你正经工作过一样，你知道的，这就是一份工作。”

sentences.en: It was a job. You were working, you were showing up, you were doing a good job.” And nine times out of 10 the person says, “Oh that’s lying, and I can’t do that.” And I have to orient them into saying, “Look everybody is beefing up their resume.” So dealing with the resume, making a creative resume is one thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一份工作。你在工作，你按时出勤，你干得很好。”十有八九那个人会说，“哦，那是撒谎，我可做不到。”而我必须引导他们说，“听着，每个人都在美化自己的简历。”所以处理简历、制作一份富有创意的简历是一回事。

sentences.en: But when you leave sex work, you also face this issue about taking a huge pay cut.
sentences.zh: 但当你离开性工作时，你还得面对收入大幅缩水的问题。

sentences.en: They will probably never make that kind of money again.
sentences.zh: 他们可能再也挣不到那种钱了。

sentences.en: We spoke to someone, Maya, who is a former prostitute who now works as a booker, as a manager.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了一位名叫 Maya 的女士，她曾是一名性工作者，现在是一名预订员兼经理。

sentences.en: She schedules and screens appointments for other sex workers in Tucson, Arizona.
sentences.zh: 她在亚利桑那州图森市为其他性工作者安排和筛选预约。

sentences.en: And, so a lot of women find themselves going back to sex work when they don’t really want to, you know, myself included.
sentences.zh: 所以，很多女性发现自己不得不重操旧业，尽管她们其实并不想这样，你知道的，包括我自己。

sentences.en: Even booking, I don’t really want to book anymore, but it’s very, very hard to go from making 300 dollars an hour to making 25 dollars an hour, which would be decent pay in the real world.
sentences.zh: 甚至连做预订，我其实也不想再做了，但要从每小时挣300美元变成每小时挣25美元，这在现实世界里虽然算是不错的薪水，但跨度实在太大了。

sentences.en: So, Sudhir you’ve talked to baseball players who were reluctant to quit, even though they’re not going to make the major leagues.
sentences.zh: 所以，Sudhir，你采访过那些不愿放弃的棒球运动员，尽管他们根本进不了美国职棒大联盟。

sentences.en: You’ve talked to sex workers, some of whom are reluctant to quit, but some of whom do a really, really good job of it.
sentences.zh: 你采访过性工作者，其中有些人很不情愿退出，但也有人把这事处理得非常、非常好。

sentences.en: For those who do a good job, talk to me about how they prepare for it, and maybe how what they do we could all learn from a little bit.
sentences.zh: 对于那些处理得很好的人，跟我讲讲他们是如何为此做准备的，也许我们可以从他们的做法中学到一点东西。

sentences.en: The first thing is you’ve got to pull that Band-Aid off, and do it quickly.
sentences.zh: 第一件事就是你得像撕创可贴一样，果断地把它撕下来。

sentences.en: And the ones that are really successful in leaving a trade in which they thought that they were going to be doing for a long time, or that they had prepared for, poured a lot of hours in, you know, when they make that decision quickly, they do pretty well.
sentences.zh: 那些在离开一个她们以为自己会干很久、或者为此做好了准备、投入了大量时间的行业时非常成功的人，你知道的，当她们迅速做出决定时，她们其实做得挺不错的。

sentences.en: I think this idea of not looking back, I know it’s a clichéd expression, but so many of the people that are able to move on, just go forward.
sentences.zh: 我觉得“向前看、不回头”这个想法，我知道这有点老套，但很多能够继续前进的人，都是直接往前走。

sentences.en: And the next time I take a job, I’m going to see if at the second day, I shouldn’t be figuring out how to get the heck out of there.
sentences.zh: 而下次我找工作时，我要看看是不是到了第二天，我就该琢磨怎么赶紧从那儿脱身了。

sentences.en: I’m sure some of you, as you listen to people talk about quitting prostitution, your mind jumps the timeline and you go back and stop these women from becoming prostitutes in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，当你们听到人们谈论戒掉卖淫时，你们中的一些人脑海中的时间线会倒流，恨不得回到过去阻止这些女性一开始就去当妓女。

sentences.en: It’s like watching a horror movie where you’re saying: “No, no, no!
sentences.zh: 这就好像在看恐怖电影时你会喊：“不，不，不！

sentences.en: Don’t open that door!” But these women did open that door.
sentences.zh: 别开那扇门！”但这些女性确实开了那扇门。

sentences.en: There are, however, some places that try to get people to quit before they’ve even started.
sentences.zh: 不过，确实有些地方试图在人们还没开始之前就让他们打退堂鼓。

sentences.en: We sent Stacey Vanek Smith, a reporter for Marketplace, to get the details.
sentences.zh: 我们派了 Marketplace 的记者 Stacey Vanek Smith 去了解详细情况。

sentences.en: How much do you like your job? If someone offered you money to quit, how much would it take for you to do it?
sentences.zh: 你有多喜欢你的工作？如果有人给你钱让你辞职，你要拿多少才肯干？

sentences.en: This job is worth more than a million. Definitely.
sentences.zh: 这份工作比一百万还值钱。绝对的。

sentences.en: I love it here. It’s very hard to get in, but once you’re in, It’s kind of like the Wizard of Oz.
sentences.zh: 我爱这里。想进来很难，但一旦你进来了，这就有点像《绿野仙踪》。

sentences.en: We’re in the Emerald City … that’s what I feel like That’s Christina Gomez.
sentences.zh: 我们身处翡翠城……这就是我的感觉。那是 Christina Gomez。

sentences.en: And would you believe she’s talking about a job that pays just a few bucks above minimum wage?
sentences.zh: 你敢相信吗，她谈论的是一份只比最低工资高出几美元的工作？

sentences.en: The job is at Zappos, an online shoe store that Amazon paid almost a billion dollars for in 2009.
sentences.zh: 这份工作是在 Zappos 做的，这是一家在线鞋店，亚马逊在 2009 年花近十亿美元买下了它。

sentences.en: At an employee training session in Las Vegas, everybody talked like that.
sentences.zh: 在拉斯维加斯的一次员工培训会上，每个人都这么说。

sentences.en: Most of the 35 people in my session were headed to the company’s call center, where they will earn about eleven dollars an hour, dealing with customer questions and complaints.
sentences.zh: 我那场培训里的35个人大部分都要去公司的呼叫中心，在那里他们每小时能赚大约十一美元，处理客户的疑问和投诉。

sentences.en: But as it trains these new hires, Zappos also throws them a curve ball.
sentences.zh: 但在培训这些新员工的同时，Zappos 也给他们出了个难题。

sentences.en: Here’s Marcela Gutierrez, a trainer with the Zappos.
sentences.zh: 这是 Zappos 的培训师 Marcela Gutierrez。

sentences.en: Remember how we said, that we want this to be more than a job for you guys, we want it to be a career, we want it to be a calling for everybody.
sentences.zh: 还记得我们说过吗，我们希望这对你们来说不仅仅是一份工作，我们希望它是一项事业，我们希望它成为每个人的天职。

sentences.en: I’m here to offer you $3,000 if you decide that this is not the right place for you.
sentences.zh: 我来这里是想向你提供3,000美元，如果你决定这里不适合你的话。

sentences.en: It’s known around Zappos as The Offer During Training — when these new employees are already being paid, Zappos offers 3,000 dollars to any new hire who wants to walk away from the job.
sentences.zh: 在 Zappos，这被称为“培训期间的Offer”——当这些新员工已经在拿工资时，Zappos 会向任何想要离职的新员工提供3,000美元。

sentences.en: It’s been going on for a few years, and it’s … gotten some press.
sentences.zh: 这已经持续好几年了，而且……引起了一些媒体关注。

sentences.en: But secret or no, what is the company thinking?
sentences.zh: 但不管保密与否，这家公司的葫芦里卖的是什么药？

sentences.en: I put that question to company CEO Tony Hsieh, who masterminded The Offer.
sentences.zh: 我把这个问题抛给了公司首席执行官 Tony Hsieh，他是这个 Offer 的幕后策划者。

sentences.en: It’s really putting the employee in the position of,”Do you care more about money or do you care more about this culture and the company?’” And if they care more about the easy money then we probably aren’t the right fit for them.
sentences.zh: 这其实是把员工置于这样一种境地：“你更在乎钱，还是更在乎这里的文化和公司？”如果他们更在乎容易到手的钱，那我们可能就不适合他们。

sentences.en: Zappos talks about its culture a lot. And Hsieh says that culture is enough to keep people from taking an offer anywhere else, or Zappos’ offer to leave.
sentences.zh: Zappos 经常谈论它的企业文化。Hsieh 表示，这种文化足以让人不接受其他任何地方的 Offer，也不会接受 Zappos 的离职 Offer。

sentences.en: And when I say culture, I’m not just talking about free soda in the break room and casual Fridays, as I discovered on the company tour with Zappos Supervisor Loren Becker.
sentences.zh: 当我谈到文化时，我指的不仅仅是休息室里的免费苏打水和休闲星期五，正如我在与 Zappos 主管 Loren Becker 一起参观公司时发现的那样。

sentences.en: So we’ve entered the main, building. So we can like officially start our real tour.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经进入了主建筑。这样我们就可以正式开始真正的参观了。

sentences.en: Everybody’s wearing sneakers and T-shirts, there are sign-up sheets for picnics and poker groups.
sentences.zh: 每个人都穿着运动鞋和 T 恤，有野餐和扑克俱乐部的报名表。

sentences.en: Conference rooms are decorated in outer space and “under the sea” themes.
sentences.zh: 会议室被装饰成太空和“海底”主题。

sentences.en: It looks like the convergence of seven difference holidays.
sentences.zh: 这看起来就像七个不同的节日汇聚在了一起。

sentences.en: It definitely does. You’ll see that everybody’s desk is decorated different.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。你会发现每个人的办公桌都装饰得各不相同。

sentences.en: There are knick-knacks, rubber duckies, streamers.
sentences.zh: 有小摆设、小黄鸭、彩带。

sentences.en: It’s pretty crazy. People are so excited to join the “crazy,” they turn down the free money.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。人们对加入这份“疯狂”感到如此兴奋，以至于他们拒绝了免费的钱。

sentences.en: Out of the nearly two thousand people Zappos has trained, the company says only about 30 have ever taken the offer.
sentences.zh: 在 Zappos 培训过的近两千人中，公司称只有大约30人接受了这个 Offer。

sentences.en: Christina Gomez is one of those people. remember her?
sentences.zh: Christina Gomez 就是其中之一。还记得她吗？

sentences.en: It’s kind of like the Wizard of Oz. We’re in the Emerald City, that’s what I feel like.
sentences.zh: 这有点像《绿野仙踪》。我们在翡翠城，这就是我的感觉。

sentences.en: Turns out, a week after I talked with her, Gomez took the offer.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，在我采访她一周后，Gomez 接受了那个 Offer。

sentences.en: I called her up to ask her what pulled the curtain back.
sentences.zh: 我打电话给她，问是什么拉开了这层帷幕。

sentences.en: It was very cult-like place. It was the honeymoon period and then I started getting comfortable at Zappos and then I started seeing some of the things that I didn’t really like about it, and so we broke up.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常像邪教的地方。那是蜜月期，然后我开始在 Zappos 感到安逸，接着我开始看到一些我其实并不喜欢的东西，所以我们分道扬镳了。

sentences.en: Gomez says The Offer wasn’t the main reason she quit.
sentences.zh: Gomez 说这个 Offer 并不是她辞职的主要原因。

sentences.en: She says the schedule Zappos gave her didn’t work with her child care and another job she has at Apple.
sentences.zh: 她说 Zappos 给她的排班无法兼顾她的育儿需求以及她在苹果公司的另一份工作。

sentences.en: But how big an incentive is The Offer? Three thousand dollars equals two months of busting your hump in a call center.
sentences.zh: 但这个 Offer 的诱惑力有多大？三千美元等于你在呼叫中心拼死拼活干两个月的工资。

sentences.en: The fact almost no one takes it, just doesn’t make sense.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有人接受这个事实，实在是说不通。

sentences.en: It does, however, make sense to Dan Ariely, a behavioral economist at Duke who studies decision-making.
sentences.zh: 不过，对于研究决策行为的杜克大学行为经济学家 Dan Ariely 来说，这完全说得通。

sentences.en: He says that easy money is actually not so easy.
sentences.zh: 他说，这笔轻而易举到手的钱其实并不那么容易拿。

sentences.en: The reason that this trick works is that people spend 10 days, they become a part of the family.
sentences.zh: 这个把戏之所以管用，是因为人们花了10天时间，他们成为了这个大家庭的一部分。

sentences.en: Zappos is all about making trainees feel like family.
sentences.zh: Zappos 的核心就是让实习生感觉像家人一样。

sentences.en: There are happy hours and scavenger hunts and team projects.
sentences.zh: 这里有欢乐时光、寻宝游戏和团队项目。

sentences.en: And after all that — and before you’ve started actually working … you get The Offer.
sentences.zh: 在经历这一切之后——在你真正开始工作之前……你收到了这个 Offer。

sentences.en: And it’s a limited-time thing. When it expires, it’s real power kicks in, says Ariely.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个限时活动。Ariely 说，当它过期时，真正的威力就开始显现了。

sentences.en: There’s something called cognitive dissonance.
sentences.zh: 有一种东西叫做认知失调。

sentences.en: It says that if you’ve acted in a certain way, over time, you’re going to overly justify your behavior.
sentences.zh: 意思是如果你以某种方式行事，随着时间的推移，你会过度地为主张自己的行为寻找合理的解释。

sentences.en: So the next morning after you rejected the 3,000 dollars, you’re going to wake up and say, “My goodness, I really must love this company if I rejected this amount.” Translation: We like suffering for things we love; we like it so much, that if we suffer for something, we will actually decide we must love it.
sentences.zh: 所以，在你拒绝了3,000美元的第二天早上，你会醒来说：“天哪，既然我拒绝了这么多钱，那我一定真的很爱这家公司。”翻译过来就是：我们喜欢为我们所爱的事物受苦；我们如此热爱，以至于如果我们为某事受苦，我们实际上会认为自己一定深爱着它。

sentences.en: Ariely says fraternities and sororities work like this — when they make rushers stand in the rain or run naked across campus, turning indignity into allegiance.
sentences.zh: Ariely 说兄弟会和姐妹会就是这样运作的——当他们让新成员站在雨中或赤身裸体跑过校园时，就把羞辱转化为了效忠。

sentences.en: Militaries, sports teams, religious cults all use this tactic too: combining our intense desire to belong with our intense desire to justify our actions.
sentences.zh: 军队、运动队、宗教邪教也都在使用这种策略：将我们对归属感的强烈渴望与我们为自己行为辩护的强烈渴望结合起来。

sentences.en: The result? A group of employees who won’t quit even if you pay them.
sentences.zh: 结果呢？培养出一群哪怕你付钱给他们也绝不辞职的员工。

sentences.en: That’s Marketplace reporter Stacey Vanek Smith.
sentences.zh: 那是 Marketplace 记者 Stacey Vanek Smith。

sentences.en: Zappos does sound a bit like a religion.
sentences.zh: Zappos 听起来确实有点像个宗教。

sentences.en: Quitting a religion is never simple. My parents were a pair of Brooklyn-born Jews who, before they met each other, both converted to Roman Catholicism.
sentences.zh: 戒掉一个宗教绝非易事。我的父母是一对在布鲁克林出生的犹太人，在他们相遇之前，两人都皈依了罗马天主教。

sentences.en: This was in the mid-1940s; my parents were in their 20s.
sentences.zh: 那是20世纪40年代中期；我父母当时20多岁。

sentences.en: As you can imagine, this conversion didn’t go over so well with their families.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的那样，这种皈依在他们的家族里并没有那么受欢迎。

sentences.en: My dad’s father declared him dead, sat shiva for him, never spoke to my father again.
sentences.zh: 我父亲的父亲宣告他已经死亡，为他坐了哀悼期，从此再也没有跟我父亲说过话。

sentences.en: So I grew up in a very devout Catholic family, the eighth and youngest kid.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在一个非常虔诚的天主教家庭里长大的，我是八个孩子里最小的一个。

sentences.en: And then, when I was in my 20s, I quit Catholicism.
sentences.zh: 然后，当我20多岁的时候，我退出了天主教。

sentences.en: Went back to Judaism. My mother took it hard, but not nearly as hard as my dad’s father took it when he converted.
sentences.zh: 重新回到了犹太教。我母亲对此很难接受，但远没有我父亲在我皈依时那么难以接受。

sentences.en: Anyway, I’ve always been pretty interested in religious quits.
sentences.zh: 总之，我一直对宗教退出事件相当感兴趣。

sentences.en: My name is Saloma Miller Furlong. I am the author of a new memoir called Why I Left the Amish.
sentences.zh: 我叫 Saloma Miller Furlong。我是一本名为《我为什么离开阿米什人》的新回忆录的作者。

sentences.en: I’m Emma Gingerich, and I go to college at Tarleton State University in Stephenville, Texas.
sentences.zh: 我是 Emma Gingerich，我在德克萨斯州斯蒂芬维尔的特尔顿州立大学上大学。

sentences.en: And right now I’m also working on finishing up my book and getting it published.
sentences.zh: 目前我也在努力完成我的书并将其出版。

sentences.en: And what is your book called, Emma? Runaway Amish Girl.
sentences.zh: 你的书叫什么名字，Emma？《逃跑的阿米什女孩》。

sentences.en: I wanted to speak to Emma Gingerich and Saloma Furlong because quitting a religion like the Amish seems especially traumatic, with the religion, family, and community all mixed up.
sentences.zh: 我想和 Emma Gingerich 以及 Saloma Furlong 聊聊，因为离开像阿米什人这样的宗教似乎格外痛苦，宗教、家庭和社区全都交织在了一起。

sentences.en: When you look back at the decision you made, which was a big one, to quit your religious lifestyle and religious community, talk to me about the price that you feel you paid or the benefit that you gained.
sentences.zh: 当你回看你做出的那个决定——一个重大的决定，即放弃你的宗教生活方式和宗教社区时，跟我聊聊你觉得你付出的代价或者你获得的益处。

sentences.en: When I think of costs I think of the things that I miss.
sentences.zh: 当我想起代价时，我想到了那些我怀念的事物。

sentences.en: And definitely the community atmosphere of knowing your place in the community is part of the costs.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，那种社区氛围——清楚自己在社区中的地位——就是代价的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, the church gatherings where they sing the Amish chants and feeling like there’s a sense of legacy almost in that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们唱着阿米什圣歌的教堂聚会，以及其中几乎带有一种传承感的感觉。

sentences.en: But the upside of it is there have been so many times, so many moments in my life when I knew that quitting the Amish was the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 但好的一面是，在我的生命中有那么多的时光，那么多的时刻，让我知道离开阿米什人是正确的事情。

sentences.en: One example was on May 29th of 1982 when I walked into the church sanctuary at Christ Church Presbyterian on the Redstone campus and saw my husband-to-be standing there in a blue tuxedo waiting for me to come up to the altar.
sentences.zh: 其中一个例子是在 1982 年 5 月 29 日，当我走进红石校区基督长老会教堂的圣殿，看到我未来的丈夫穿着蓝色燕尾服站在那里等我走向圣坛时。

sentences.en: That moment encapsulated just how I was doing the right thing.
sentences.zh: 那一刻完美地诠释了我做的是多么正确的事。

sentences.en: That was literally the happiest day of my life.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是我一生中最快乐的一天。

sentences.en: So, Emma, if you could just describe as briefly as you want, kind of, your childhood, you know, your family growing up and getting to the point where you decided to leave, and why and how that happened.
sentences.zh: 所以，Emma，如果你能尽可能简短地描述一下你的童年，你知道的，你成长中的家庭，以及你是如何走到决定离开的那一步的，为什么以及这一切是如何发生的。

sentences.en: My family used to make baskets and we would take them every Friday and sell them at a little town close to a busy highway.
sentences.zh: 我的家人过去常常编织篮子，我们每个星期五都会把它们带到一个靠近繁忙高速公路的小镇上去卖。

sentences.en: And sometimes it would be me and my sister.
sentences.zh: 有时候只有我和我姐姐。

sentences.en: We did a lot of things that we weren’t supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 我们做了很多我们本不该做的事情。

sentences.en: But there was … around 15 was the time when I started thinking about how I would be if I would leave the Amish.
sentences.zh: 但大约在15岁的时候，我开始思考如果我离开阿米什人，我的生活会是什么样。

sentences.en: And you know, sitting there selling baskets you see a lot of people coming and we used to look at cars and look at all the different colors, and try and pick which one we would want if we would ever leave the Amish.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，坐在那里卖篮子，你会看到很多人来来往往，我们过去常常看汽车，看所有不同的颜色，并试图挑选如果我们离开阿米什人会想要哪一辆。

sentences.en: Did it feel like you became a different person?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这就像你变成了另一个人吗？

sentences.en: Are you the same person who just needed a change of scenery?
sentences.zh: 你还是那个只是需要换个环境的同一个人吗？

sentences.en: I guess what I really want to know is what was the cost to you of quitting the Amish?
sentences.zh: 我想知道的其实是，离开阿米什人对你来说代价是什么？

sentences.en: What were the downsides? And what were the upsides?
sentences.zh: 有什么不好的地方？又有什么好的地方？

sentences.en: Well the downsides would be leaving the family and knowing that nothing’s going to be the same again when you go back home to visit.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不好的地方就是离开家庭，并且知道当你回家探亲时，一切都将不复从前。

sentences.en: And the upside is yes, you are a different person.
sentences.zh: 而好的一面是，是的，你变成了一个不同的人。

sentences.en: You become…to me, I became somebody else, which was good for me.
sentences.zh: 你变成了……对我来说，我变成了另一个人，这对我有好处。

sentences.en: How old are you now? 23. And do you have regrets about leaving?
sentences.zh: 你现在多大？23岁。你对离开有什么遗憾吗？

sentences.en: No. Zero? Not at all. Saloma Furlong is in her 50s, and now lives in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 没有。零？完全没有。Saloma Furlong 现在50多岁了，住在马萨诸塞州。

sentences.en: Not long ago, she did an informal survey of the Amish community where she grew up, in Geauga County, Ohio.
sentences.zh: 不久前，她对她长大的阿米什社区（位于俄亥俄州吉奥加县）进行了一次非正式调查。

sentences.en: Out of about 2,500 households, she estimates some 170 individuals left the community.
sentences.zh: 在大约2,500户家庭中，她估计大约有170人离开了社区。

sentences.en: So quitting isn’t common, but it’s not like it never happens either.
sentences.zh: 所以退出虽然不常见，但也不是说从来没有发生过。

sentences.en: Furlong says her father was mentally ill and violent; and that, ultimately, is what led her to leave.
sentences.zh: Furlong 说她的父亲患有精神疾病并且有暴力倾向；而这，最终促使她选择了离开。

sentences.en: My life was so unbearable that the fear of the known was greater than my fear of the unknown.
sentences.zh: 我的生活实在是太难熬了，以至于我对已知事物的恐惧超过了对未知事物的恐惧。

sentences.en: So, for me, it’s a matter of, “Are you happy the way you are?
sentences.zh: 所以，对我来说，这是一个问题：“你现在的状态快乐吗？

sentences.en: And if not, then quit what you’re doing.” It’s that simple for me.
sentences.zh: 如果不快乐，那就放弃你正在做的事。”对我来说就这么简单。

sentences.en: You make it sound so easy, I’m wondering have you quit other things in life besides the Amish?
sentences.zh: 你把它说得这么容易，我在想除了阿米什人，你还放弃过生活中的其他事情吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yes. Do you want me to get started? Yes please.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。你想让我开始说吗？好的，请说。

sentences.en: I’ve quit jobs that were not satisfactory.
sentences.zh: 我辞过那些不满意的工作。

sentences.en: I quit my bakery business when I realized after 10 years of punching bread dough that it was never going to talk back to me and that it was intellectually a desert.
sentences.zh: 我在揉了10年面包面团后发现它永远不会对我回应，而且在智力上犹如一片荒漠时，我关掉了我的面包店生意。

sentences.en: Let’s see, what else have I quit? I quit a church community one time.
sentences.zh: 让我想想，我还放弃过什么？我曾经退出过一个教会社区。

sentences.en: So, yes, I’m a serial quitter. And it’s worked for me, what can I say?
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我是一个连续退出者。这对我挺管用的，我能说什么呢？

sentences.en: You’re a gold medal quitter; you’re not just a serial quitter.
sentences.zh: 你是个获得金牌的退出者；你不仅仅是个连续退出者。

sentences.en: You’re a champion. So, but let me ask you this, in retrospect were all of these quits good?
sentences.zh: 你是个冠军。所以，让我问你这个，回过头来看，所有这些退出都是好事吗？

sentences.en: Yes. They were. All right, so you really need to be like a quitting coach, don’t you?
sentences.zh: 是的。它们都是。好吧，所以你真的需要成为一名退出教练，对吧？

sentences.en: You need to travel around the world and tell people, look at this situation, why are you still in this, why are you stuck in this?
sentences.zh: 你需要环游世界，告诉人们，看看这情况，你为什么还呆在这儿，为什么陷在这里面出不来？

sentences.en: Do you think that’s a future calling of yours perhaps?
sentences.zh: 你认为这可能是你未来的某种天职吗？

sentences.en: Somebody just asked me that the other day about being a counselor and I said, “Nope it’s not something I want to do.” Because you’d just quit anyway.
sentences.zh: 前几天刚有人问过我关于当咨询师的事，我说，“不，这不是我想做的事。”因为你反正也会退出的。

sentences.en: You might be right.
sentences.zh: 你可能是对的。

sentences.en: “A quitter never wins and a winner never quits.” In 1937, a self-help pundit named Napoleon Hill included that phrase in his very popular book Think and Grow Rich.
sentences.zh: “半途而废者永不成功，成功者永不半途而废。”1937年，一位名叫 Napoleon Hill 的自助励志大师在他的畅销书《思考致富》中写下了这句话。

sentences.en: Hill was inspired in part by the rags-to-riches industrialist Andrew Carnegie.
sentences.zh: Hill 的灵感部分来自于白手起家的实业家 Andrew Carnegie。

sentences.en: These days the phrase is often attributed to Vince Lombardi, the legendarily tough football coach.
sentences.zh: 如今，这句话经常被归功于传奇而严厉的美式橄榄球教练 Vince Lombardi。

sentences.en: What a lineage! And it does make a lot of sense, doesn’t it?
sentences.zh: 多么深厚的传承！这确实很有道理，不是吗？

sentences.en: Of course it takes tremendous amounts of time and effort and, for lack of a more scientific word, stick-to-itiveness, to make any real progress in the world.
sentences.zh: 当然，要在世界上取得任何真正的进展，需要投入大量的时间、精力和——用一个不够科学的词来说——坚持不懈的精神。

sentences.en: But time and effort and even stick-to-itiveness are not in infinite supply.
sentences.zh: 但时间、精力甚至坚持不懈都不是取之不尽用之不竭的。

sentences.en: Remember the opportunity cost: Every hour, every ounce of effort you spend here cannot be spent there.
sentences.zh: 记住机会成本：你在这里花费的每一个小时、每一分力气，都无法用在别处。

sentences.en: So let me counter Napoleon Hill’s phrase with another one, certainly not as well known.
sentences.zh: 所以我要用另一句话来反驳 Napoleon Hill 的名言，这句肯定没那么出名。

sentences.en: It’s something that Stella Adler, the great acting coach, used to say: Your choice is your talent.
sentences.zh: 那是伟大的表演教练 Stella Adler 常说的一句话：你的选择就是你的天赋。

sentences.en: So choosing the right path, the right project, the right job or passion or religion — that’s where the treasure lies; that’s where the value lies.
sentences.zh: 所以选择正确的道路、正确的项目、正确的工作、激情或宗教——这才是宝藏所在；这才是价值所在。

sentences.en: So if you realize that you’ve made a wrong choice — even if already you’ve sunk way too much cost into it — well, I’ve got one word to say to you, my friend: Quit.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你意识到自己做出了错误的选择——即使你已经在其中投入了过多的沉没成本——好吧，我只想对你这个朋友说一句话：退出吧。
